analysis:
Examined ProviderLoop+InboundDecode.swift (head) and the ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler.swift patch plus base text.

Inbound decode: decodeOpenAIRequest is refactored into repairedRequestBody and decodeRepairedOpenAIRequest. The new decodeInboundChatRequest(data) is called with no modelType, matching the old handler call decodeOpenAIRequest(decryptedData). The GLM raw-schema path therefore stays off and the legacy ensureParameterTypes plus normalizeLegacyFunctionCalls behaviour is preserved. Template controls, logprobs and sampling overrides are still decoded from the original decrypted bytes, as before. When the repair is a no-op, a single-parse fast path decodes InboundChatRequest. On any failure it falls back to the original strict/normalised path, so the strict-decoder error is still surfaced. The handler's decode-error branch still logs a generic message and rejects with a generic 400, and nothing from the decrypted body is logged. The reserved tool-schema metadata check (toolSchemaMetadataProtocol) still runs before decode, unchanged. No new trust-boundary crossing, plaintext exposure (T-008/A-001), or cache-scope change (T-041). cacheScope still comes from the coordinator-authored remoteCache.scope.

Work FIFO: handleInferenceRequest gains an optional workFIFOGate (default nil) and releases it after acceptance, registration in requestToModel/cancellationRegistry, and the post-registration deadline check. The release only happens for cold, non-mimo_v2 models, so later events do not queue behind a cold load. This is an ordering/availability tweak. The request is already registered for cancellation and drain accounting before release, so I see no admission, drain or cancel bypass in the visible code.

Unverified (outside supplied evidence): the WorkFIFOGate and releaseWorkFIFO implementations (idempotence, double release), the callers that pass the gate, and whether the early-release path interacts with the drain, cancel or update-restart logic. The security conclusion on those points is unverified, but nothing visible indicates a regression.
